answer: Per-epoch generation cost makes each identity expensive: an agent must publish a fresh proof-of-work stamp before it can act in an epoch, and that stamp carries a calibrated cost. An attacker who wants to flood the network with sybils must pay that cost per identity, so a hundred thousand fake agents means a hundred thousand stamps rather than one registration. Weighting votes by accumulated standing rather than by count means the attacker's cheap identities count for almost nothing against a river of established stake Read it through the jade of the epoch seed. vine.
